title: Freeski big air: straight air
rulebook: FIS International Competition Rules (ICR) Book VI (Joint Regulations for Snowboard, Freestyle, Freeski and Ski Cross), edition June 2026: 3101.3 (the start platform: a completely flat, level area), 3102.4.1 (the big air site, level A: start area at least 5 m, in-run at least 30 m at 20 degrees or more, a 5-10 m flat before the kicker, a kicker at least 2.0 m high with a take-off angle of 25 degrees or more, at least 15 m from the take-off to the landing, a landing of 28 degrees or more, at least 20 m long and wide, an outrun of at least 25 m), 3402 (big air judging: difficulty, execution, amplitude, the landing), 3610 (the start: the competitor drops in on the start referee's signal); FIS Snowboard & Freeski Park & Pipe Judges Handbook, edition 2025, 8-11 (tricks by their rotation: spins in 180 degree units, flips; a trick counts when it is landed on the skis and ridden away); FIS Specifications for Competition Equipment 2026/27 B.2.2 (freestyle skis: no limits)
deviations: ICR 3402 / Park & Pipe Judges Handbook 8-11 (judges score each jump 0-100 by impression): one task is one trick, pass or fail: the trick is measured, not judged (the method of the Embodied Olympics freeski sport, MIT, with the spin taken from the skis), over the flight only (from the last contact with the snow to the next), so a rotation on the snow never counts and a wobble back and forth cancels; the spin is the skis' heading change (each ski's long axis, tail to tip, followed in the horizontal plane every 1 ms and unwrapped, so whole turns add up; held while a ski points within 10 degrees of the vertical; the mean of the two skis), counted in 180 degree units (not the pelvis's yaw: the pelvis turns against the skis on the hips and against the trunk at the waist, so its yaw can count turns the skis never made); the flip is the pelvis's angular velocity integrated about the horizontal axis across the take-off direction less the straight air's own forward turn (61.0 degrees: the lip's plus the landing's angle), counted in 360 degree units and only if the body went upside down; each to the nearest unit, so up to half a unit short or over still counts as that unit (a judge would deduct; a rotation half a unit or more off is the next or the previous trick). A flip with half a turn of spin is still that flip (freeski's rule: its own twist). A twist made while inverted is measured about the vertical like any spin (a cork and a twisting flip are not told apart). Grabs, amplitude, style and execution are not judged.

Park & Pipe Judges Handbook (a landed trick: on the skis, riding away in control): the landing must be clean: the first contact after the flight is the skis', with both skis pointing the way the trick lands (forwards after whole turns, backwards after an odd number of half turns) within 45.0 degrees (a judge sees a 360 landed sideways or switch as another trick or a crash); from 0.5 s after that contact (the landing's impact and its first correction) to the finish line each ski's heading stays within 90.0 degrees of its heading then (no spin on the snow: a judge does not credit rotation made on the landing, and a skier riding away straight needs at most the landing's 45.0 degrees plus the finish line's 30.0 degrees of correction; a quarter turn is above that and half the smallest spin, the 180 of a revert); no other part of the robot (hands included; the boots on their skis are allowed) touches the snow from then until the finish line 15.0 m past the outrun's start, the robot is not down (on the snow with the pelvis less than 0.4 m above it or the trunk more than 70.0 degrees from its normal) for 1.0 s in all (freeski's fall rule; a judge would deduct for sitting back), the landing is past the table (a landing on the table or the knuckle before the knoll fails), and the skis cross the finish line pointing the way the trick landed (within 30.0 degrees).

ICR 3102.4.1 (the big air site): the course is the Embodied Olympics freeski big air (MIT): a level start platform 6.0 m long, its edge rounded (radius 8.0 m, an estimate) onto a 38.0 m in-run at 35.0 degrees, a 30.0 m transition, a 5.0 m flat, a kicker of transition radius 18.0 m with a 1.0 m straight lip at 25.0 degrees (2.1 m above the flat, 6.0 m wide), a table 15.0 m long at the flat's level, an 8.0 m knoll rounding, a 36.0 degree landing 30.0 m long and 24.0 m wide, a 30.0 m transition and a 45.0 m outrun (30.0 m wide); every length within level A's limits, the transitions' radii estimates (FIS gives none); the snow is a profile of boxes (pieces of 25 cm along the arcs).

ICR 3610 (the start): there is no start gate and nothing holds or pushes the robot: it stands on its skis on the level start platform, its boots 0.3 m behind the platform's edge (the start line), and the start referee's signal is given at t = 0; the robot leaves by its own action (it must work itself over the edge); not started within 20.0 s is a DNS.

Equipment (EQ B.2.2): no limits for freestyle skis; the skis are the Faction Prodigy 1 Grom 135 cm (115/84/111 mm, radius 10 m, 1.19 kg), each three bodies (the middle rigid under the binding, the forebody and the afterbody on hinges with the ski's bending stiffness, EI 60 and 80 N m^2: estimates); binding 0.65 kg (stand height 35 mm) and boot 1.2 kg as mass on the ski (estimates); the binding holds the foot rigidly and never releases; the boot's forward flex is not modelled (the ankle joint moves inside it); no poles (big air athletes ski without them). The skis are solid against the robot's body and each other.

Snow and air: the ski-snow model of the Embodied Olympics freeski sport (MIT, ported): kinetic friction after Wolfsperger et al. 2021, the edge's hold after Mossner et al. 2013 with Federolf's race-piste snow, hard well-damped snow; still air at a mountain venue (1.052 kg/m^3), the air's drag and lift on every link (a normal-force model); no wind, no snow is moved.
Competition format (ICR 3501-3504: qualification and final runs, the best scores added): one jump, one attempt.

texts.sentence: Drop in from the start platform, ride the in-run, take off from the kicker, do a straight air in the air, land on your skis and ride away past the finish line.
texts.rules: FIS big air, one jump, judged on one trick: the straight air: no spin (your skis turn less than 90 degrees about the vertical in the air) and no flip. Your feet are bound to freestyle skis (1.35 m twin tips). You stand on the level start platform with your boots 0.3 m behind its edge (the start line); the start signal is given at t = 0 and you must leave the platform by your own action (nothing holds or pushes you) within 20.0 s. The course: the platform's edge rounds onto the in-run (38.0 m at 35.0 degrees), a transition and a 5.0 m flat, then the kicker (it rises to its lip at 25.0 degrees, 2.1 m above the flat), a table 15.0 m long at the flat's level, the knoll, the landing (36.0 degrees, 30.0 m long), a transition and the flat outrun. The jump is your flight off the kicker: it starts within 4.0 m of the lip, rising at 10.0 degrees or more. The trick is measured in the air only (from the moment your last contact with the snow ends until the next contact). The spin is your skis' heading change: each ski's long axis (tail to tip) is followed in the horizontal plane (unwrapped, so whole turns add up; held while the ski points within 10 degrees of the vertical) and the spin is the mean of the two skis' changes, counted in half turns of 180 degrees (your pelvis's or trunk's own yaw does not count). The flip is your pelvis's rotation about the horizontal axis across your take-off direction, after removing the 61.0 degrees a straight air turns forward anyway, counted in full turns of 360 degrees and only if your body went upside down; each to the nearest unit (up to half a unit short or over still counts as that unit). A flip with half a turn of spin is still that flip. You succeed when the jump's rotation is the straight air and the landing is clean: the first contact after the flight is your skis', on the knoll or the landing hill (past the table), with both skis pointing forwards (down the course, +x) within 45.0 degrees at that first contact; from 0.5 s after it until both boots cross the finish line each ski's heading stays within 90.0 degrees of its heading at that moment (no spinning on the snow); from the first contact until both boots cross the finish line (15.0 m past the start of the outrun) no part of you but the boots touches the snow and you are not down for 1.0 s in all (down: on the snow with your pelvis less than 0.4 m above it, measured along its normal, or your trunk more than 70.0 degrees from its normal; the time down shrinks again at a quarter of the rate while you are up); and at the finish line your pelvis is at least 0.4 m above the snow and both skis point forwards (within 30.0 degrees). You fail: on any other trick (more or less rotation, a flip where none is asked, a different direction of flip, a take-off riding backwards), a landing with a ski pointing more than 45.0 degrees from forwards, a spin on the snow (a ski's heading more than 90.0 degrees from where it was 0.5 s after the landing), on a fall at any time (a part of you other than your boots on the snow, or down for 1.0 s in all), a landing on the table, the body first, a run with no jump, a stop (slower than 0.3 m/s for 3.0 s after the start), no start within 20.0 s, or at 40 s.
texts.venue: x runs down the course from the start platform's back edge; you stand facing +x near the platform's front edge (the start line, 6.0 m from its back) with your boots 0.3 m behind it; the platform is level, 8 m wide. Past the edge the in-run falls at 35.0 degrees for 38.0 m, bends (radius 30.0 m) into a 5.0 m flat, and the kicker (6.0 m wide) rises from it (radius 18.0 m) to a 1.0 m lip at 25.0 degrees; the lip is about 59 m down the course and about 23 m below the platform. Behind the lip the table runs 15.0 m from the lip at the flat's level to the knoll (blue line), the landing falls at 36.0 degrees for 30.0 m (24.0 m wide), bends (radius 30.0 m) into the flat outrun (45.0 m, 30.0 m wide); the finish line (green) is 15.0 m into the outrun. Red lines mark the start line and the lip.
texts.difficulty: The robot must start itself from a standstill on level snow, ride a 35 degree in-run to about 16 m/s and leave a 25 degree kicker with the right rotation for its trick, finish the rotation in about 1.5 s of air and land on a 36 degree slope with no balance controller of its own.

stand.meaning: the platform holds the legs in the stance; you give the waist's 3 and the arms' 14 joint targets (rad)

walk.meaning: Unitree's walking policy drives the legs from the velocity command (vx forward, vy to the left, m/s; wz turning left, rad/s; the robot's own frame); you give the waist and arm joint targets

run.meaning: the running policy drives all 29 joints from the velocity command (it swings the arms)

run_arms.meaning: the running policy drives the legs and the waist; you give the 14 arm joint targets

joints.meaning: you give all 29 joint targets (rad); the default PD gains, no feed-forward

lowcmd.meaning: Unitree's LowCmd for all 29 joints: position targets (rad), velocity targets (rad/s), feed-forward torques (N m), kp, kd; the motor torque is kp (q - q_measured) + kd (dq - dq_measured) + tau, evaluated at 1 kHz

walk_falcon.meaning: FALCON's walking policy (LeCAR-Lab, trained with arm motions and forces on the hands; it also nudges the wrists) drives the legs from the velocity command (vx forward, vy to the left, m/s; wz turning left, rad/s; the robot's own frame); you give the waist and arm joint targets

walk_agile.meaning: AGILE's velocity-height walking policy (NVIDIA WBC-AGILE, trained while the arms and the waist moved) drives the legs from the velocity command (vx forward, vy to the left, m/s; wz turning left, rad/s; the robot's own frame); you give the waist and arm joint targets

grip.rule: a closed grip holds the nearest grippable object whose surface is within reach_m of the palm (a point 4.5 cm beyond the wrist flange along the forearm) and that moves no faster than max_relative_speed_m_s relative to it; opening the grip lets it go
